title: Farm / Shadow Source Expansion II — Reputation, Memory, Anti-Fandom, Context Collapse & High-Control Dynamics
purpose: Extend the Farm/Sektur/Moloch source base into reputation theory, anti-fandom, negative parasocial relationships, context collapse, deplatforming, gossip/punishment and high-control/self-sealing-group analysis. These sources support only their stated empirical or scholarly claims and do not validate Potatoverse supernatural mappings.

sources.topic: negative parasocial relationships and anti-fan communities
sources.source: Mardon, Cocker & Daunt 2023 — When parasocial relationships turn sour
supports: positive parasocial relationships can become negatively charged
anti-fan communities can sustain negative parasocial ties
eroded/exploitative intimacy can motivate anti-fan participation
sources.project_use: Supports the hypothesis that dislike can maintain rather than terminate attention and relational investment.

sources.source: Oxford Handbook of Parasocial Experiences — Beyond Friendship: A Call for Research on Non-amicable Parasocial Relationships
supports: negative parasocial relationships are diverse
ludic/ironic parasocial relations can derive pleasure from disparagement
hatewatching and anti-fandom are not simply absence of relationship
sources.project_use: Provides vocabulary for the Cow/observer relation without assuming hatred is equivalent to disengagement.

sources.source: Feinberg, Cheng & Willer 2012 — Gossip as an effective and low-cost form of punishment
supports: gossip spreads reputational information
gossip can function as efficient low-cost punishment
gossip can promote cooperation and social control
sources.project_use: Supports Farm-as-reputation-infrastructure and the distinction between legitimate norm enforcement and weaponized reputational extraction.

sources.source: Gossip Versus Punishment: The Efficiency of Reputation to Promote and Maintain Cooperation
supports: gossip can facilitate reputation spreading
gossip can promote trust and cooperation
reputational mechanisms can substitute for more costly punishment
sources.project_use: Shows that gossip is not intrinsically shadow-like; moral valence depends on truthfulness, proportionality, context and downstream consequences.

sources.topic: gossip and reputation in everyday life
sources.source: Gossip and reputation in everyday life
supports: gossip affects reputation
gossip can reduce social standing and partner choice
gossip can enable indirect punishment and exclusion
sources.project_use: Supports measurable reputation-edge effects rather than treating gossip as mere speech volume.

sources.source: Marwick & boyd 2011 — I tweet honestly, I tweet passionately
supports: social media collapses multiple audiences into shared contexts
users manage imagined audiences
self-presentation changes under networked visibility
sources.project_use: Supports the archive concept that fragments may be reinterpreted outside the audience and context that originally shaped them.

sources.source: One Size Fits All: Context Collapse, Self-Presentation Strategies and Language Styles on Facebook
supports: disparate audiences become conjoined
network size/heterogeneity affect self-presentation
context collapse has measurable behavioral effects
sources.project_use: Adds empirical support to context-collapse mechanisms in identity and archive interpretation.

sources.source: Vu, Hutchings & Anderson 2023 — No Easy Way Out
supports: Kiwi Farms deplatforming case study
rapid platform displacement and traffic fragmentation
activity and traffic reductions without total disappearance
network resilience and migration
sources.project_use: Supports modeling Swamp/Farm as a network topology that can migrate rather than a single domain or owner.

sources.topic: bounded choice and self-sealing high-control groups
sources.source: Lalich 2004 — Bounded Choice: True Believers and Charismatic Cults
supports: bounded choice framework
charisma and commitment in high-control groups
behavior can become internally rational within increasingly constrained social structures
sources.project_use: Feature-based comparator only; not evidence that an online community is a cult.

sources.source: Lalich 2026 — Brainwashing Versus Free Choice: Responsibility for Criminal Acts by Cult Members
supports: charismatic authority
transcendent belief system
systems of control
systems of influence
self-sealing/closed-system formulation
sources.project_use: Provides explicit variables for high-control comparison while preserving the distinction between feature analysis and cult diagnosis.

supports: cult is a controversial social-science concept
the term changed across scholarly traditions
ordinary use is often pejorative
sources.project_use: Supports the archive rule to prefer observable high-control/self-sealing features over blanket cult labels.

sources.source: Song, Molho & Van Lange 2026 — Gossip or confrontation?
supports: gossip, exclusion and confrontation are distinct informal sanctions
perceived norm-severity affects sanction appropriateness
sanction choice has reputational consequences for punishers
sources.project_use: Adds a two-sided reputation model: Farm processes not only target reputation but also the reputation/status of punishers and enforcers.

new_relational_deductions: Target reputation and punisher reputation should be stored as separate directional effects.
A negative parasocial relationship can create continued dependence on the target for content, ritual viewing and group bonding.
Context collapse creates a translation problem: one artifact can enter many audiences whose norms differ from the audience for which it was produced.
Deplatforming should be represented as a topology change rather than a binary on/off event.
High-control analysis should attach to observable relations—leader centrality, dissent cost, exit cost, control and influence—not to pejorative group labels.
Gossip has both Garden and Swamp possibilities: accurate reputational warning can protect a group; distorted or non-correctable gossip can become durable Mud.
archive_rule: Do not promote a psychological or sociological comparator into a diagnosis of a named person or group. Record observed behavior first, comparator second, Potatoverse symbolic interpretation third.
